title: Transformers cache strategies trade compilation, capacity and latency
summary: Dynamic, static, offloaded and quantized KV caches have different contracts; select by workload and API support rather than a universal ranking.

hardware: Device and quantization-backend support must be checked for the chosen model; this is API guidance
software: huggingface/transformers at 2126f65b0ab267e113e78a002447fc7094de83d5; later revisions need reinspection
conditions: Autoregressive generation with known length distribution, attention type and memory budget

claims.description: StaticCache reserves a maximum size and supports compilation, at the cost of reserved capacity and work on masked positions for shorter sequences.
The inspected table distinguishes sliding-layer, offloading and torch.compile support. Quantized cache can hurt latency on short contexts with sufficient GPU memory; offload adds transfer work.

downstream_impact: vLLM and vLLM-Omni: audit model/cache adapters when Transformers changes; its generate cache_implementation flags do not configure vLLM paged KV managers.
vllm-ascend: test supported cache backends independently and retain model-specific sliding/chunked-attention behavior.
recommendations: Treat downstream impact as an OmniRSI transfer hypothesis, not an upstream compatibility or performance result.
validation_plan: Test mixed prompt lengths, prefix reuse and sliding/chunked layers with separate per-request cache state.
Measure memory, TTFT and decode latency along with long-context output quality and compile behavior.
limitations: Memory reduction alone is not throughput evidence.
This source documents Transformers interfaces; downstream serving-cache compatibility remains an unverified transfer hypothesis.
Point-in-time source extraction, not a historical commit-delta audit. No local accelerator or model-quality reproduction was run.
